Radiance Fields: Elements and Morphs

A radiance field says, at every point of space, how much light is stopped there and what light leaves it. Surfaces, clouds, point splats and neural scenes are all ways of writing one down.

iori1

1Jorik Jonathan Chase, 3DIE — Design, Art & Technologies Label. Paper 0.2 of a series, a companion to paper 0 and paper 0.1. October 2026.

The paper in one paragraph

The Fractal Engine was designed around one object: a radiance field, a density and a colour at every point, read by a camera along its rays. This paper takes that object apart. A ray through a density shows how a pixel is made, and how a hard surface is just a very steep density. A point that sends different colours in different directions shows what view dependence costs. One shape, stored four ways at the same budget (voxels, a grid of distances, Gaussians, the lowest frequencies), shows what each representation keeps and loses: on our test shape the grid of distances is two to four and a half times more accurate than voxels for the same numbers stored. Then the morphs: between representations (a surface becomes a cloud, a cloud becomes splats, the engine draws one fractal both ways) and between shapes, where mixing densities, mixing distances and moving Gaussians give three different in-betweens.

The first four figures are drawn in the page, in two dimensions so every quantity can be seen; drag in them and turn their sliders. The others are the engine, started when they scroll into view; click or tap one to take the controls, press outside to give the page back its scroll. The mathematics sits folded in boxes marked The mathematics.

1. What a Radiance Field Is

Two functions of space: a density σ(x), how much light is stopped at x, and a radiance c(x, d), the light x sends toward direction d. A picture is what arrives along each ray.

Light crossing a cloud is dimmed by everything it passes and joined by what the cloud gives off. Kajiya and Von Herzen wrote this down for rendering in 1984, and Max collected the forms it takes [1] [2]. NeRF made the same integral the thing to learn: fit σ and c so that the integral along every camera ray reproduces a set of photographs [3]. Everything since, including Gaussian splatting, is a choice of how to store σ and c, and how to evaluate the integral fast.

The Fractal Engine fits here. Its pull mode marches a distance estimate to a surface and lights it, its push mode throws Gaussian splats, its fog and glow are density and emission between the camera and the surface. Paper 0's fractals and the engine's formulas are generators of radiance fields; this paper is about the fields.

2. Density and the Ray

A pixel is a weighted sum of the colours along its ray. The weights are how much light survives to a point times how much is stopped there.

Follow a ray from the eye. The transmittance T(t) is the share of light from distance t that still reaches the eye: it starts at one and falls wherever the density is. The point at t contributes its colour with weight T(t)·σ(t). Where the field is thin the weights are spread out and the ray sees through; where it is dense the weights pile up at the first thing the ray meets and nothing behind it counts.

A surface is the limit of that. Give a shape's distance field d(x) a density that rises steeply across d = 0, σ = s·logistic(−s·d), and turn s up: the cloud thickens into a skin, and the weights along the ray collapse into a spike at the surface [4] [5]. The engine's pull mode lives at that limit: sphere tracing finds where the distance reaches zero [6], and its fog and glow are what a finite density adds in front of the surface.

The mathematics

Along r(t) = o + t·d, with T(t) = exp(−∫0t σ(r(u)) du),

C = ∫0∞ T(t) σ(r(t)) c(r(t), d) dt,   opacity = 1 − T(∞).

With samples ti spaced δi and the field taken constant between them (NeRF's quadrature),

C ≈ Σi Ti αi ci,   αi = 1 − e−σiδi,   Ti = Πj<i(1 − αj).

For σs = s·logistic(−s·d) and a ray crossing d = 0 at t* with unit speed, the weight T·σs tends to δ(t − t*) as s → ∞: the integral returns the colour at the surface.

3. Emission and Direction

A matte point sends the same colour everywhere. A glossy one sends a different colour toward each direction, and that costs numbers.

The radiance c(x, d) depends on the direction d. Storing it as a table per point is out of the question, so fields store a short series in direction: spherical harmonics, the sines and cosines of the sphere [7]. Degree 0 is one number per colour channel, the matte point. Each further degree adds sharper lobes: highlights that swing as the camera moves. Plenoxels and 3D Gaussian splatting both stop at degree 3 [8] [9], which is why a splat carries 48 colour numbers and only 11 for everything else.

The mathematics

In 2-D, c(φ) = a0 + Σl=1L (al cos lφ + bl sin lφ): 2L + 1 numbers per channel. On the sphere, c(d) = Σl≤L Σ|m|≤l klm Ylm(d): (L + 1)² per channel, 16 at L = 3. Truncating at degree L keeps the angular frequencies up to L and blurs sharper reflections; the engine's lamp-lit surfaces have none of this yet (section 7).

4. One Field, Four Representations

Store the same shape in the same number of numbers four ways, and measure what each gets wrong.

  • Voxels: the density on a grid, read between cells by interpolation. Plenoxels store a sparse grid; sparse bricks keep only cells near anything [8] [10].
  • A distance grid: the same cells hold the distance to the surface instead, and the edge is drawn from it [11]. Distance changes linearly across an edge, so interpolating it is nearly exact; a density jumps, so interpolating it smears.
  • Gaussians: a sum of soft ellipses, each with a centre, a shape and a weight. Splatting draws them straight to the screen [12] [9]. Here they are placed by clustering, without the gradient descent 3D Gaussian splatting runs.
  • The lowest frequencies: the field's Fourier series, kept up to the budget. A NeRF's positional encoding feeds exactly these sines and cosines to its network [13]; hash grids replace them with learned tables at many scales [14].

Mean error over the square, measured on shape A. Two things stand out. The distance grid is two to four and a half times more accurate than voxels at every budget, which is why distance fields keep returning in neural rendering. And the error falls at different rates: the distance grid and the frequencies by more than ten times for sixteen times the numbers, voxels by six, Gaussians placed without optimisation by only two. Their limit is the placement, not the form; optimised splats do far better, at the price of the optimisation.

The mathematics

Each representation is read as an occupancy o(x) ∈ [0, 1] and compared with the shape's o*(x) = logistic(−d(x)/w), w = 0.02, by the mean of |o − o*| on a 64 × 64 grid. Voxels: an n × n grid of o*, bilinear, n² = budget. Distance grid: an n × n grid of d, bilinear, then logistic. Gaussians: k = budget/6, k-means on the shape's cells, each cluster's covariance Σ and weight n·a/(2π√|Σ|), the sum clipped at 1. Frequencies: the 2-D DFT of o* on 64², the lowest |k| first, two numbers each.

5. Morphs Between Representations

A field can be carried from one representation to another, and each carry loses something different.

  • Distance → density: the sharpness of section 2. A finite s turns any distance field into a cloud; NeuS and VolSDF learn s with the rest [4] [5].
  • Density → Gaussians: fit ellipses to where the density is (section 4), or, as the engine does, sample the attractor and give each sample the Gaussian its walk carried. The engine writes those as a 3D Gaussian splatting file.
  • Gaussians → image: project each ellipse to the screen and blend front to back [12].
  • Distance → mesh: sample the distance on a grid and extract the zero surface, by marching cubes or surface nets [15] [16]; the engine exports a mesh this way.

The engine draws one fractal both ways. Pull treats the Sierpiński tetrahedron as a distance field and marches to its surface; push walks its attractor backwards and lays down a Gaussian at every sample, each shaped by how the walk squeezed space. Same set, two representations, switched by one key.

6. Morphs Between Shapes

Halfway between two shapes depends on the representation you take the halfway point in.

Mix two densities and you get a crossfade: both shapes at half strength, a ghost of each. Mix two distance fields and you get a shape in between, whose edge moves continuously from one to the other and may change topology on the way [17] [18]. Move the Gaussians of one shape onto the Gaussians of the other and the mass travels, the way optimal transport interpolates distributions [19] [20]. Three in-betweens of the same two shapes, all different.

The engine has a fourth way, which no stored field has: change the generator. Breeding moves a formula's parameters, so every frame between two fractals is itself a fractal of the same family; a chimera blends two formulas inside the iteration (paper 0.1). And the collage's morph join, (1 − w)·a + w·b on two distance estimates, is the middle column of this figure applied to finished fractals.

The mathematics

Density mix: ot = (1 − t)oA + t oB. Distance mix: dt = (1 − t)dA + t dB, a valid bound on the distance to its zero set when both are (the mix of two 1-Lipschitz functions is 1-Lipschitz), drawn as logistic(−dt/w). Gaussian transport: each pair (μA, ΣA, wA) → (μB, ΣB, wB) moved linearly; between two Gaussians the optimal-transport path moves Σ along the Bures geodesic instead, which the linear form approximates when the shapes are close.

7. What the Engine Has, and Has Not

Read as a radiance field, the engine is a generator with two renderers and three exports.

  • Has: a density in its hard-surface limit (pull), the same set as Gaussians (push), emission as a shading network over the orbit's readings, fog and glow as a thin density in front, and exports as splats, mesh and images.
  • Has not: view-dependent emission (its surfaces are lit by a lamp, not given spherical harmonics); a finite density inside the fractal (a cloud of the set rather than its skin); a stored field to fit to photographs. The sparse bricks of the design and paper 0's landscapes are where those would live.
  • Open: the engine's representations at equal budget, measured as section 4 measures shape A; a morph between two fractals in distance, in Gaussians and in the generator, side by side, as section 6 does in 2-D.
